correctness.rationale: The Thue form reduces modulo p to one affine line, and all first partial derivatives are divisible by p, so its value modulo p^2 is constant on each residue class modulo p. An exact verifier checks every class for all 84 residual exponents with two arithmetic evaluations and finds precisely the stated 31 primes with unique compatible class (1,0). The cited Katz-Pratt reductions then imply y == -1 (mod p) and x == +/-1 (mod p^2).

originality.rationale: Katz-Pratt formulate local triviality as Conjecture 8.1, prove only nonvanishing modulo p in Proposition 8.2, and leave an unspecified factor in the q=p, s>1 case of their local Thue count. Searches of the equation, local-triviality formulation, prime-square conclusion, equivalent Thue formulation, and the current SCOPE archive did not locate this criterion or 31-prime result. Originality remains to the best of our knowledge, with residual risk from very recent literature.

value.rationale: The result proves the stated local-triviality conjecture for 31 of the 84 prime exponents left by known global reductions, strengthens x modulo p to modulo p^2, and gives a reusable exact criterion for further exponents in the same Thue family.
